question: What is a fiscal year?
evidence: 12 consecutive months ending on the last day of any month except December 31st
reference_answer: A fiscal year is 12 consecutive months ending on the last day of any month except December 31st.

question: What is a calendar year for tax purposes?
evidence: 12 consecutive months beginning on January 1st and ending on December 31st
reference_answer: 12 consecutive months beginning on January 1st and ending on December 31st.

question: What is a short tax year?
evidence: A short tax year is a tax year of less than 12 months
reference_answer: A tax year of less than 12 months, required when the entity is not in existence for an entire tax year or changes its accounting period.

question: In which cases must a taxpayer adopt the calendar year?
evidence: You keep no books or records
reference_answer: If you keep no books or records, have no annual accounting period, your present tax year does not qualify as a fiscal year, or a provision of the Internal Revenue Code or Treasury Regulations requires it.

question: What is an improper tax year?
evidence: Taxpayers that have adopted an improper tax year must change to a proper tax year
reference_answer: A tax year that is not permissible, e.g. a business that began on March 15 and adopted a tax year ending on March 14. The taxpayer must change to a proper tax year (amended return with Form 1128 for a calendar year, or Form 1128 for a fiscal year).

question: Which form do you file to request IRS approval to change your tax year?
evidence: you must file Form 1128 to request IRS approval to change your tax year
reference_answer: Form 1128. No user fee is required if you qualify for an automatic approval request.

question: What is a principal partner?
evidence: A principal partner is one who has a 5% or more interest
reference_answer: A partner who has a 5% or more interest in the profits or capital of the partnership.

question: Which tax year must a partnership use when partners with the same tax year own a majority interest?
evidence: a majority interest (more than 50%) in partnership profits and capital
reference_answer: If one or more partners with the same tax year own more than 50% of partnership profits and capital, the partnership must use the tax year of those partners.

question: What tax years are permitted for an S corporation?
evidence: must use a permitted tax year
reference_answer: The calendar year, a tax year elected under section 444, a 52-53-week tax year ending with reference to the calendar year or a section 444 year, or any other tax year for which the corporation establishes a business purpose.

question: How do you make a section 444 election?
evidence: Make a section 444 election by filing Form 8716
reference_answer: By filing Form 8716 with the IRS Service Center where the entity will file its return, and attaching a copy to Form 1065, 1120S or 1120 for the first tax year of the election.

question: When must a partnership or S corporation with a section 444 election make a required payment?
evidence: is more than $500
reference_answer: For any tax year the election is in effect and the required payment for that year (or any preceding year) is more than $500. It is made with Form 8752, due by May 15 of the following calendar year.

question: What is constructive receipt of income?
evidence: Income is constructively received when an amount is credited to your account or made available to you without restriction
reference_answer: Income is constructively received when it is credited to your account or made available to you without restriction, even if you do not have possession of it. It is not constructively received if your control is subject to substantial restrictions.

question: What is the gross receipts test for using the cash method?
evidence: average annual gross receipts for the 3 prior tax years were $26 million or less
reference_answer: A corporation or partnership (not a tax shelter) meets the test if its average annual gross receipts for the 3 prior tax years were $26 million or less (indexed for inflation).

question: What is the function test for a qualified personal service corporation?
evidence: at least 95% of its activities are in the performance of services
reference_answer: At least 95% of its activities must be services in health (including veterinary), law, engineering (including surveying and mapping), architecture, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, or consulting.

question: When is the all events test met for income under an accrual method?
evidence: all events have occurred which fix your right to receive the income
reference_answer: When all events have occurred which fix your right to receive the income and you can determine the amount with reasonable accuracy.

question: When does economic performance occur for interest expense?
evidence: Economic performance occurs with the passage of time
reference_answer: With the passage of time (as the borrower uses the lender's money), not as payments are made.

question: When can an employer take a current deduction for vacation pay?
evidence: if you pay it during the year or, if the amount is vested
reference_answer: If paid during the year or, if vested, within 2 and a half months after the end of the year. Otherwise it is deducted in the year actually paid.

question: What does the FIFO inventory method assume?
evidence: assumes the items you purchased or produced first are the first items you sold
reference_answer: That items purchased or produced first are the first items sold, consumed or disposed of; closing inventory is matched with the costs of the most recently purchased or produced items.

question: How do you adopt the LIFO method?
evidence: File Form 970, Application To Use LIFO Inventory Method
reference_answer: File Form 970 (or a statement with the same information) with your timely filed tax return for the first year you use LIFO.

question: How does a trade discount affect the cost of inventory?
evidence: You must reduce the cost of inventory by a trade (or quantity) discount
reference_answer: A trade (or quantity) discount, allowed regardless of when payment is made, must reduce the cost of inventory.

question: Our company closes its books every June 30 rather than at the end of December. What kind of accounting period is that?
evidence: 12 consecutive months ending on the last day of any month except December 31st
reference_answer: A fiscal year: 12 consecutive months ending on the last day of any month other than December.

question: A company that follows the January-December year shuts down for good in late July. What period does its last return cover?
evidence: period from January 1 through July 23
reference_answer: A short period from January 1 through the date of dissolution (July 23 in the IRS example).

question: My uncle passed away in the spring. What is the deadline for submitting his last return?
evidence: by the 15th day of the 4th month after the close
reference_answer: By the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of his regular tax year (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). The final return covers January 1 to the date of death.

question: The bank added interest to my savings in December but I only noticed it in January. For which year do I declare it?
evidence: You must include the amount in gross income for 2021
reference_answer: For the year it was credited and made available (December's year), because it was constructively received then, even if not withdrawn or recorded.

question: I paid for a three-year business insurance contract upfront. Can I write off the whole amount in the first year?
evidence: effective for 3 years (36 months)
reference_answer: No. The 12-month rule does not apply; the cost is spread over the years it covers ($500, $1,000, $1,000, $500 for $3,000 starting July 1).

question: I received pens and paper plus the bill in December but settled it in January. Using accrual accounting, which year do I claim the cost?
evidence: You can deduct the expense in 2020 because all events have occurred to fix the liability
reference_answer: In December's year: the liability is fixed, the amount is determinable, and economic performance occurred when the supplies were received.

question: Prices keep going up. Which way of costing my stock makes my ending stock value smaller?
evidence: LIFO will produce a larger cost of goods sold and a lower closing inventory
reference_answer: LIFO: during inflation it gives a larger cost of goods sold and a lower closing inventory than FIFO.

question: Some of my products got scratched and are out of fashion, so I can't sell them at the normal price. How do I value them?
evidence: bona fide selling price minus direct cost of disposition
reference_answer: At their bona fide selling price minus the direct cost of disposition, whatever method is used for the rest of the inventory (raw materials or partly finished goods: on a reasonable basis, not below scrap value).

question: I found an arithmetic mistake in my books. Do I need the tax authority's permission to fix it?
evidence: Correction of a math or posting error
reference_answer: No. Correcting a math or posting error is not a change in accounting method and does not require IRS approval.

question: A self-employed painter buys canvases and paint for her work. Must she add those costs to the value of her paintings instead of deducting them?
evidence: freelance authors, photographers, and artists are exempt from the uniform capitalization rules
reference_answer: No, if she qualifies: freelance artists are exempt from the uniform capitalization rules for qualified creative expenses.

question: What is the difference between the cash method and an accrual method for reporting income?
evidence: all items of income you actually or constructively received
you generally report income in the year it is earned
reference_answer: Cash method: income is included when actually or constructively received. Accrual method: income is reported in the year it is earned (all events test), regardless of when payment is received.

question: Which methods can be used to identify the cost of inventory items, and which methods can be used to value inventory?
evidence: You can use any of the following methods to identify the cost of items in inventory
generally available for valuing inventory
reference_answer: Identifying cost: specific identification, FIFO, LIFO. Valuing: cost, lower of cost or market, retail.

question: How can a partnership avoid using its required tax year, and which form is used for each option?
evidence: The partnership can establish a business purpose for a different tax year
Make a section 444 election by filing Form 8716
reference_answer: By a section 444 election (Form 8716), a 52-53-week tax year ending with reference to its required year or a section 444 year, or by establishing a business purpose (Form 1128).

question: Under the retail method, how is the average markup percentage computed, and what is the closing inventory at cost in the IRS example?
evidence: The result is the average markup percentage
Divide the markup by the total retail value
reference_answer: Total retail value minus total cost, divided by total retail value (35,000 / 140,000 = 25%). Closing inventory at retail $42,000 minus 25% markup ($10,500) gives $31,500 at cost.

question: When can a recurring expense be deducted before economic performance, and does this exception cover workers' compensation?
evidence: An exception to the economic performance rule allows certain recurring items
This exception does not apply to workers
reference_answer: If the all-events test is met, economic performance occurs by the earlier of 8 and a half months after year end or the timely return filing date, the item is recurring and treated consistently, and it is immaterial or gives a better match with income. It does not apply to workers' compensation or tort liabilities, where economic performance occurs as payments are made.
